title: Tiny Pieces, Big Trouble: The Plastic That Never Really Leaves the Sea
title_zh: 微小的碎片，巨大的麻烦：从未真正离开海洋的塑料
intro_zh: 本文约 539 词，CET-4 难度，含 6 个重点词（debris, swallow, accumulate, consume, fragile, crucial），适合练习主旨、细节、推断与词义题。

paragraphs.en: In 1997, a sailor named Charles Moore was sailing home across the Pacific Ocean when he noticed something strange: plastic bottles, caps and fishing nets floating around his boat, day after day, hundreds of miles from the nearest city. He had accidentally found what scientists now call the Great Pacific Garbage Patch, a huge area of ocean where gentle currents gather waste from many countries at once.
paragraphs.zh: 1997年，一位名叫查尔斯·摩尔的帆船手正驾船穿越太平洋返航，这时他注意到一件怪事：塑料瓶、瓶盖和渔网日复一日地漂在他的船周围，而这里离最近的城市有数百英里。他无意中发现了如今科学家所说的“太平洋大垃圾带”——一片巨大的海域，温和的洋流把来自许多国家的垃圾汇聚到一起。

paragraphs.en: Many people imagine a solid island of rubbish there. In fact, most of the patch cannot be seen. Sunlight, salt and waves slowly break plastic into smaller and smaller pieces. Any piece shorter than five millimetres is called a microplastic. This debris can float for decades and travel thousands of kilometres.
paragraphs.zh: 很多人以为那里是一座实心的垃圾岛。事实上，垃圾带的大部分是看不见的。阳光、盐分和海浪慢慢把塑料分解成越来越小的碎片。任何小于五毫米的碎片都被称为微塑料。这些碎片能在海上漂浮几十年，漂移数千公里。

paragraphs.en: Sea animals do not read labels. Fish, shrimp and even tiny plankton mistake the colourful bits for food and swallow them. A 2019 study found microplastics in the stomachs of fish caught in nearly every ocean. Researchers have also found them in Arctic ice, in mountain rain, and in the water coming out of our taps. Nobody knows exactly how much plastic is floating out there, but some estimates run into the millions of tonnes.
paragraphs.zh: 海洋动物不会看标签。鱼、虾甚至微小的浮游生物都会把这些五颜六色的碎片误当成食物吞下去。2019年的一项研究发现，在几乎每个大洋捕获的鱼的胃里都有微塑料。研究人员还在北极的冰、山区的雨水以及从我们水龙头里流出的水中发现了它们。没有人确切知道海上漂着多少塑料，但有些估计达到数百万吨。

paragraphs.en: When a small fish eats plastic, the plastic does not disappear. Larger fish eat those small fish, and the particles accumulate inside their bodies. This means people who regularly consume seafood may also take in a small amount of plastic. Scientists are still studying how harmful this is, but most agree that reducing plastic in the sea matters for our health.
paragraphs.zh: 小鱼吃下塑料后，塑料并不会消失。大鱼吃掉这些小鱼，颗粒便在它们体内不断累积。这意味着经常吃海鲜的人也可能摄入少量塑料。科学家仍在研究这有多大危害，但大多数人认为，减少海洋中的塑料对我们的健康是有影响的。

paragraphs.en: The scale of the problem is easy to underestimate. Most of the waste starts as something we use only once: bags, cups, packaging and bottles. The United Nations estimates that about eleven million tonnes of plastic enter the ocean every year, which is like emptying one rubbish truck into the sea every minute. A plastic bottle needs roughly 450 years to break down completely. By 2040, without action, the amount could almost triple.
paragraphs.zh: 这一问题的规模很容易被低估。大部分垃圾最初都只是我们只用一次的东西：袋子、杯子、包装和瓶子。联合国估计，每年约有1100万吨塑料进入海洋，相当于每分钟往海里倒一卡车垃圾。一个塑料瓶大约需要450年才能完全降解。如果再不采取行动，到2040年这个数量几乎会翻三倍。

paragraphs.en: Wildlife pays the price first. Seabirds feed plastic pieces to their chicks without knowing, and many chicks do not survive. Turtles mistake floating bags for jellyfish. Lost fishing nets, called ghost nets, continue to catch fish for years. Plastic also carries harmful chemicals that can enter the bodies of the animals that eat it. Even coral, already fragile, is easily damaged by plastic that blocks sunlight.
paragraphs.zh: 最先付出代价的是野生动物。海鸟在不知情的情况下把塑料碎片喂给雏鸟，许多雏鸟因此活不下来。海龟会把漂浮的塑料袋误认成水母。遗失的渔网——被称为“幽灵网”——会持续捕鱼多年。塑料还携带有害化学物质，会进入吃下它的动物体内。就连本就脆弱的珊瑚，也很容易被遮挡阳光的塑料伤害。

paragraphs.en: Yet there is real progress. Such efforts play a crucial part, even though they cannot solve the problem alone. A Dutch project called The Ocean Cleanup has built long floating barriers that collect plastic while letting fish swim underneath. Its river machines, named Interceptors, catch rubbish before it reaches the sea. In 2008, Rwanda became one of the first countries to ban thin plastic bags, and its capital is now noticeably cleaner. In Kenya, plastic bags were banned in 2017, and many shoppers now carry cloth bags without thinking twice. More than 100 countries have since passed similar laws.
paragraphs.zh: 不过也有实实在在的进展。这些努力发挥着关键作用，尽管单靠它们无法解决问题。荷兰的一个名为“海洋清理”的项目建造了长长的浮动屏障，在收集塑料的同时让鱼从下面游过。它的河道机器名为“拦截者”，能在垃圾入海之前将其截住。2008年，卢旺达成为最早禁止薄塑料袋的国家之一，其首都如今明显更干净了。在肯尼亚，塑料袋于2017年被禁止，许多购物者现在会毫不犹豫地自带布袋。此后已有100多个国家通过了类似的法令。

paragraphs.en: Scientists say the answer is not only cleaning up, but producing less. Choosing a reusable bottle, refusing a plastic straw and joining a local beach clean all help, even if the effect of one person seems small. The sea has carried our waste quietly for decades; it is time we carried the responsibility instead.
paragraphs.zh: 科学家说，答案不只是清理，而是少生产。选择一个可重复使用的水瓶、拒绝一根塑料吸管、参加一次当地的净滩活动，这些都有帮助，哪怕一个人的作用看起来很小。几十年来，海洋一直默默承载着我们的垃圾；现在该轮到我们承担责任了。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How a sailor discovered a floating island of rubbish.
Why plastic waste in the ocean is a growing problem and what is being done about it.
Why fish in the Pacific Ocean are becoming smaller.
How to build machines that clean up rivers.
questions.explain: 全文从发现太平洋垃圾带谈起，说明塑料在海中如何破碎、进入食物链并危害生物，最后介绍治理措施，因此 B 最全面。A 只是开头的引子；C 文中并未提及鱼变小；D 只是第七段的一个细节。

questions.q: According to the passage, what happens to most plastic in the ocean?
options: It is eaten by seabirds within a few years.
It sinks to the bottom and disappears.
It is gradually broken into tiny pieces by sunlight, salt and waves.
It is collected by ships from more than 100 countries.
questions.explain: 第二段明确指出阳光、盐分和海浪把塑料分解成越来越小的碎片，故 C 正确。A、B 与原文不符；D 是对第七段立法的曲解，文中并未说船只收集垃圾。

questions.q: What can be inferred from the last two paragraphs?
options: Individual actions make no difference at all.
Both technology and government policy play a part in reducing plastic waste.
Rwanda was the first country to ban all plastic products.
The Ocean Cleanup has already removed all the plastic from the sea.
questions.explain: 最后两段既提到技术手段（浮动屏障、拦截者河道机器），也提到政府立法（卢旺达、肯尼亚及100多个国家），可推断两者都在发挥作用，故选 B。A 与末段“这些都有帮助”相矛盾；C 中卢旺达禁止的是薄塑料袋，并非所有塑料制品；D 过于绝对。

questions.q: The word 'accumulate' in Paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: accumulate 意为“积累、聚积”，与 build up 意思最接近。break down 意为“分解”，give off 意为“散发”，wash away 意为“冲走”，均与上下文不符。
